Use case: scientific-educational.
Create ONE finished landscape 3:2 educational illustration for a Korean beginner CS article, replacing a dense technical diagram with an intuitive everyday visual metaphor. High quality editorial picture-book style: soft rounded shapes, clean ivory background, teal and blue accents, generous whitespace, no watermark, no unnecessary decoration. Large crisp Korean labels, very little text; not a slide with boxes of paragraphs.
Topic: process versus thread. Main visual: TWO distinct cutaway workshop rooms with clearly separated walls. Left room labelled "프로세스 A": exactly TWO friendly workers labelled "스레드 1" and "스레드 2", sharing ONE central workbench and supply shelf labelled "공유 자원". Each worker carries a separate small task notebook labelled "개인 스택". Right room labelled "프로세스 B": ONE worker and its OWN workbench and supplies, clearly separated from room A. No path sharing resources between the two rooms. Small visual legend at bottom: "프로세스 = 작업실" and "스레드 = 작업자". Heading "프로세스와 스레드". Footer "같은 작업실의 자원은 함께, 작업 기록은 각자".
Make relationships understandable at a glance, readable at mobile width. This is a metaphor: do not imply independent memory protection between threads within one room. Entire output is one image, not multiple files.

Title exactly "둘이 더했는데 왜 1일까?"
Three clearly numbered panels left to right. Panel 1 "① 둘 다 0을 읽음": teal worker A and blue worker B both look at ONE shared counter display "0", each holding their own small note with "0". Panel 2 "② 각자 1을 계산": each person's own note now says "0 + 1 = 1". Panel 3 "③ 같은 값으로 덮어씀": workers sequentially place cards both reading "1" on the SAME shared counter, show one old 1 card behind the latest 1 card and final shared display "1", not two counters. Small footer "기대: 2   실제: 1". Single concise takeaway "읽기부터 쓰기까지 한 번에 보호해야 해요". Make it clear BOTH operations increased by one but stale reads cause lost update; no implication the mathematical sum 1+1 is 1. Exactly three panels within a single image.

Title exactly "TCP 연결: 세 번의 확인".
Make a large friendly laptop character labelled "클라이언트" on left and server character labelled "서버" on right. THREE vertically ordered message lanes between them, with envelopes and unambiguous arrows. First lane arrow points LEFT TO RIGHT, label "① SYN", short speech "연결할 준비 됐나요?". Second lane arrow points RIGHT TO LEFT, label "② SYN + ACK", short speech "네! 제 준비도 확인해 주세요.". Third lane arrow points LEFT TO RIGHT, label "③ ACK", short speech "확인했어요!". Do NOT draw padlocks or imply encryption. No numerical sequence numbers in this image. Exactly three messages, no fourth handshake. Single image.

Title "DNS는 인터넷 주소 안내소".
Left a friendly laptop asking "www.example.com은 어디죠?". Center a teal helpful librarian / guide labelled "재귀 리졸버", holding a small notebook labelled "캐시". Right THREE separate vertically stacked directory desks labelled exactly "① 루트", "② .com", "③ 권한 DNS". From center guide to each desk a separate clearly paired query/return connection, numbers indicate guide asks the desks IN ORDER. Root returns a sign ".com으로 가세요", .com returns a sign "담당 서버로 가세요", authoritative DNS returns a large address card "IP 주소". The USER communicates only with the central guide; do NOT show the user contacting all three desks itself, and do not show the root directly knowing the final IP. Show address card delivered from guide back to laptop. Footer "유효한 캐시가 있으면, 저장한 답을 바로 써요". Keep simple, readable. Label this as metaphor with small text "캐시가 없는 조회의 비유". No fake concrete IP addresses.
